crafts.name: Pipe Cleaner
crafts.tagline: Bend, twist, and create anything you imagine
crafts.description: Pipe cleaner crafting, also known as chenille stem crafting, is a wonderfully tactile and forgiving art form perfect for all ages. These fuzzy, flexible wires can be twisted, coiled, and sculpted into an endless variety of shapes — from delicate flowers and whimsical animals to intricate 3D sculptures. What makes pipe cleaner crafts so special is their accessibility: no special skills required, mistakes are easily undone, and the materials are inexpensive and widely available.
benefits: Highly forgiving — mistakes are easily fixed

crafts.name: Crochet
crafts.tagline: Loop by loop, stitch by stitch — create something magical
crafts.description: Crochet is an ancient textile craft using a hooked needle to interlock loops of yarn, thread, or other materials. Unlike knitting which uses two needles, crochet uses a single hook — making it arguably easier to pick up and more portable. From cosy blankets and wearable fashion to adorable amigurumi toys and intricate lacework, the scope of crochet is breathtaking. It is also scientifically shown to reduce anxiety, improve focus, and boost serotonin — making it as good for the mind as it is for the hands.

crafts.name: Fuse Beads
crafts.tagline: Pixel art you can hold in your hands
crafts.description: Fuse beads (also called Perler beads, Hama beads, or melty beads) are small plastic beads placed on pegboards and fused together with heat from an iron. The result is a rigid, colourful plastic tile that perfectly mimics pixel art. This craft beautifully bridges digital art and physical making — if you can design it on a grid, you can make it with fuse beads. From retro video game sprites and rainbow animals to intricate mosaic portraits and functional coasters, the possibilities are limited only by your imagination and patience.
benefits: Teaches colour theory and pixel art
Easy to learn, hard to master

tools.name: Fuse Beads
tools.description: Available in 1000+ colours. Standard size (5mm) for most projects, midi size (5mm Hama), mini (2.6mm) for fine detail. Brands: Perler, Hama, Artkal.

tools.name: Pegboards
tools.description: Come in square, round, hexagon, and specialty shapes. Large boards allow bigger designs; interlocking boards for massive projects.

tools.name: Ironing Paper
tools.description: Parchment or the supplied wax paper placed over beads before ironing. Never use regular paper — it will stick.

tools.name: Household Iron
tools.description: Set to medium heat (no steam). Iron in slow circles — avoid pressing down too hard to prevent flat beads.

tools.name: Tweezers
tools.description: For placing individual beads precisely and fixing mistakes without disturbing neighbours.

tools.name: Sorting Trays
tools.description: Colour-sorted organiser trays speed up building significantly.
